title: Week 1 Assessment: Foundations
intro: This assessment checks whether you can apply the week's ideas on goals, time, English, reading, discipline and stress in realistic situations. Part A is auto-graded from your completed lessons. Part B asks you to decide, role-play and write. Take your time and answer as you would in real life.

items.prompt: It is 9 pm. You planned two hours of SQL practice today, but you spent the evening on messages and have a mock test tomorrow at 10 am. What is the best move?

options.text: Skip practice and hope the test goes well.
options.feedback: Hope is not a preparation plan.

options.text: Do a focused 50-minute block now on the weakest topic, phone away, and plan the rest for early morning.
options.feedback: A short focus block on the weak area is realistic and effective.
Sleep loss will hurt tomorrow's performance.

options.text: Move the test to next week without asking.

items.why: A realistic recovery plan protects sleep and uses focus on the weakest topic.

items.setup: You are in a short mock interview and the interviewer asks you to introduce yourself. You feel nervous and your voice is shaky.

turns.they: Please tell me a little about yourself.

options.text: Um, I am, like, a student, I guess.
options.feedback: Fillers and hedges lower the impression of confidence.
options.reply: Could you tell me more about your studies?

options.text: Take one slow breath, then: "I am Deepak, an MCA student in Faridabad with a web-development background, aiming for an ABAP role."
options.feedback: A breath and a clear structured introduction show calm.
options.reply: Good. What drew you towards ABAP?

options.text: I will say everything about my whole life now.
options.feedback: Too long and unfocused for an introduction.
options.reply: That is a lot. Let us move on.

options.text: I do not know, it just seemed good.
options.feedback: A vague answer shows little preparation.

options.text: I like solving business problems with code, and ABAP is central to SAP systems used by many large companies.
options.feedback: It is specific, honest and links interest to the role.
options.reply: That is clear. How are you preparing?

options.feedback: Money alone is a weak motive to state.

turns.they: How are you preparing for the role?

options.text: I practise daily: one focus block on ABAP basics, weekly mini programs and a written review of my errors.
options.feedback: Specific habits show discipline and a system.
This statement undermines your candidacy badly.

items.why: Calm breathing and specific, structured answers make a strong first impression.

items.prompt: Write a short plan (about 100 words) for the next two weeks that includes one specific goal, how you will break it into weekly steps, when each day you will do a focus block and a reading habit to support it.

descriptors.3: Specific and measurable with a date.
Weekly steps with daily time blocks.
A specific daily reading habit linked to the goal.

items.modelAnswer: Goal: finish 40 ABAP practice problems by 28 October. Week 1: 20 problems on internal tables and loops; week 2: 20 on database reads and review of mistakes. Daily: a 50-minute focus block at 7 pm with my phone in another room. Reading: 20 minutes every morning of ABAP documentation and notes, writing two lines of summary. I will review progress each Sunday and adjust.
items.guidance: Strong plans have a measurable goal with a date, weekly steps, specific daily times and a reading habit that supports the goal. Avoid general statements like "study more".
